Subject: Geo-differential guide + offer matrix rollout (Q4 pilot)

Team —

Sharing an initial proposal for a small Q4 pilot to operationalize geo-differentials and a standard offer matrix for IC hires (L3-L6). Goal: reduce offer cycle time while keeping total comp competitiveness across US and EU. Key points: 

- Pilot cohort: 8-10 open reqs across product and infra (US-West, US-East, Germany).
- Pricing approach: base bands + region multiplier + role premium (technical/lead).
- Outcome: standardized templates for offers, locally adjusted salary ranges, and an approval runbook to speed up finance/cc approvals.

Attached: Q4-offer-matrix-draft.xlsx (draft bands, regional multipliers, example offers). Please review the multipliers and give redline suggestions.

Ask: can everyone provide feedback by EOD Fri (10/1)? I want to surface any blocking questions before we show to Finance for pilot approval.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Talent Operations
Redwood Inference

- Suggest adding a column in the sheet for relocation/temporary allowance (we still have candidates who need this in EU).

I'll leave detailed comments in the sheet. +1 on pilot sample — smaller is better.

Thanks — good start. I've attached a short benchmarking summary that pulls market percentiles for comparable roles (US/DE/IE) — benchmark-summary-2026.pdf. A few notes from Talent Partnerships: 

- Market recommendation: target 50th-65th percentile for core IC roles during pilot to keep competitiveness but control cost.
- For leadership IC (L5+), maintain top-decile in candidate-critical markets.
- Approval path: hires <= 5% above band midpoint require Manager+TalentOps signoff; >5% needs Finance and Legal loop. Need a clear template for approvals to avoid repeated back-and-forth.

Ask: Jordan, can you draft a 1-page approval runbook (who signs, required docs, SLA for approvals) we can pilot? I can feed Finance language for the >5% cases.

Laura
Head, Talent Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: benchmark-summary-2026.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2026 14:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-differential guide + offer matrix rollout (Q4 pilot)

Folks —

Appreciate the draft. A few technical clarifications on leveling and region multipliers to avoid ambiguity in offer letters: 

- Level mapping: Please use job code mapping (see internal L3->IC3, L4->IC4) — attach mapping to final templates.
- Region multipliers (proposal): US baseline 1.00, US high-cost (SF/NY) 1.07, EU core markets (DE/IE/NL) 0.92. These are illustrative — Hannah/Laura please confirm.
- Total comp components: Base + Target Bonus + Equity; bonuses should be expressed as target % and not fixed $ in template.

Headcount/approvals: For pilot, we should route all offers above midpoint via a single Slack approval channel (#offers-approvals) plus a documented email trail. Finance needs a weekly bundle for any offers that exceed budgeted HC by team. I opened HROPS-2147 to track the runbook and approval SLA.

On quoting:
> On Fri, 01 Oct 2026 at 11:27, Laura Bennett wrote:
> > Approval path: hires <= 5% above band midpoint require Manager+TalentOps signoff; >5% needs Finance and Legal loop.

Agree — let's codify those thresholds in the runbook. I'll prototype an approval decision tree by Tue.

—Vivek
VP, People Operations
